Attempts to equate two impl subjects in a given parameter environment; after unifying them with `eq`, it scans the original and newly generated obligations and calls `negative_impl_exists` to detect a provable negative obligation, returning false when such a contradiction is found and true otherwise.

Determines whether a negative impl can discharge an obligation by first calling `resolve_negative_obligation` on the obligation itself, then elaborating super-predicates and calling `resolve_negative_obligation` on each derived obligation until one succeeds.

Attempts to prove the negation of an obligation by flipping its polarity, calling `fully_solve_obligation` to ensure the negative goal is solvable, then constructing outlives constraints and resolving regions to confirm the negated obligation is consistent.
Constructs a new `OrphanChecker` with the given type context and crate mode, initializing orphan-tracking state and an empty `non_local_tys` list.
Records a discovered non-local type by pushing it, together with whether it was found in the self type, into `non_local_tys`, then continues traversal.
Handles a parameter type during orphan checking: it continues when searching for the first local type, otherwise it stops traversal with a `ParamTy` early-exit.
Returns whether a definition should count as local for orphan checking, using `is_local` only in `InCrate::Local` mode and always returning false in remote mode.
Ignores regions during orphan checking and always continues traversal.

Implements the main orphan-check traversal over types: depending on the type kind it calls `found_non_local_ty`, `found_param_ty`, or `def_id_is_local`; for nested structure it recursively calls `visit_with`, and it early-exits when it discovers a local type or an orphan-rule violation condition.
Ignores constants during orphan checking and always continues traversal.
Trait method contract for shallow normalization of a foldable value, returning the normalized value plus any generated obligations. It does not call other methods in this list.

Implements shallow normalization for `At`: it either returns the input unchanged under the next trait solver, or creates a selection context and calls `normalize_with_depth` to normalize the value and collect obligations.
Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Ambiguous`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Error(err)` to record a selection failure; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Adds a projection candidate when possible, deduplicates identical candidates, prefers `ParamEnv` candidates over others, and otherwise converts a conflicting single candidate into ambiguity. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Handles higher-ranked projection equality by instantiating the obligation binder with placeholders inside a probe and then calling `project_and_unify_type`. It converts mismatches into `MismatchedProjectionTypes` and, when experimenting with extended GATs, filters out obligations that mention the newly created universe before returning `Holds`.

Solves a concrete projection equality by first calling `opt_normalize_projection_type` to normalize the projection, then replacing opaque types in the expected term with inference variables, and finally equating the normalized and expected terms. It returns `Holds` with accumulated obligations on success, or reports failed normalization, recursion, or mismatched projection types.

Convenience entry point for normalization at a given recursion depth: it allocates an obligation buffer, calls `normalize_with_depth_to`, and packages the normalized value together with the collected obligations.

Normalizes a foldable value into a caller-provided obligation buffer by constructing an `AssocTypeNormalizer` with `AssocTypeNormalizer::new` and then calling its `fold` method under stack protection.

Like `normalize_with_depth_to`, but uses a normalizer configured to avoid eager inference replacement: it calls `AssocTypeNormalizer::new_without_eager_inference_replacement` and then invokes `AssocTypeNormalizer::fold` under stack protection.

Checks whether a value contains projection-, inherent-, const-projection-, or optionally opaque-related type flags that require normalization, depending on the `Reveal` mode. It does not call other methods in this list.
Constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` configured for normal eager inference replacement, after asserting the old trait solver path is in use. It does not call other methods in this list.
Constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` configured to avoid eager inference replacement. It does not call other methods in this list.

Top-level normalization helper for the normalizer: it resolves inference variables, asserts there are no escaping bound vars, calls `needs_normalization` to fast-path already-normal values, and otherwise recursively folds the value.
Returns the type context for the normalizer by calling `self.selcx.tcx()`.
Enters a new binder universe, calls `super_fold_with` to recursively normalize the binder contents, then exits the universe.

Core type-normalization folder for associated types and opaque types. It first skips work when `needs_normalization` is false, otherwise recursively folds substructure with `super_fold_with`, checks recursion limits via `tcx`, and normalizes projection types by calling `normalize_projection_type` or `opt_normalize_projection_type`; it also uses bound-variable replacement and placeholder restoration around projection normalization when binders are involved.
Normalizes constants unless lazy normalization is enabled. It calls `super_fold_with` to fold nested structure, then evaluates the folded constant with `with_replaced_escaping_bound_vars` and `eval`.
Normalizes a predicate only when `allow_normalization` and `needs_normalization` both permit it; in that case it calls `super_fold_with`, otherwise it returns the predicate unchanged.

Utility that temporarily replaces escaping bound vars with placeholders before running a closure, then restores them afterward. When escaping vars are present it calls `BoundVarReplacer::replace_bound_vars`, runs the callback, and then calls `PlaceholderReplacer::replace_placeholders`; otherwise it just runs the callback directly.

Entry point for converting bound regions, types, and consts into placeholders while recording reverse mappings. It constructs a `BoundVarReplacer`, folds the input through it, and returns the rewritten value plus the collected maps.
Finds or lazily creates the universe index associated with a given de Bruijn level, extending the tracked universe stack as necessary. It does not call other methods in this list.
Returns the inference context's type context directly.
Adjusts the current Debruijn depth for a nested binder, calls `super_fold_with` to replace bound variables inside it, then restores the previous depth.

Replaces late-bound regions at or above the current binder with placeholder regions, using `universe_for` to choose the universe and `mk_region` to build the replacement; regions outside that range are left unchanged.

Replaces bound types at or above the current binder with placeholder types, calling `universe_for` and `mk_ty` for the replacement; if the type merely contains deeper bound variables, it calls `super_fold_with` to recurse, otherwise it returns the type unchanged.
Replaces bound constants at or above the current binder with placeholder constants, using `universe_for` and `mk_const`; for all other constants it calls `super_fold_with` to recurse.
Calls `super_fold_with` only when the predicate contains variables bound at or above the current binder depth; otherwise it returns the predicate unchanged.
Entry point for converting placeholders back into bound vars using previously recorded maps and universe information. It constructs a `PlaceholderReplacer` and folds the input through it.
Returns the inference context's type context directly.
Skips binders with no placeholders or infer regions; otherwise adjusts binder depth, calls `super_fold_with` to restore placeholders under the binder, and then restores the previous depth.

Resolves inference regions opportunistically, then converts mapped placeholder regions back into late-bound regions by consulting the stored universe mapping and calling `tcx().mk_region`; unmapped regions are returned as-is.

Converts mapped placeholder types back into bound types using the stored universe mapping and `tcx().mk_ty`; if the type still contains placeholders or infer regions in substructure, it calls `super_fold_with`, otherwise it returns the type unchanged.
Converts mapped placeholder constants back into bound constants via `tcx().mk_const`; for non-placeholder constants it calls `super_fold_with` to recurse.

Public entry point that normalizes an associated-type projection to a `Term`. It explicitly calls `opt_normalize_projection_type`; if that returns no concrete result due to ambiguity, it falls back to `infer_projection` to create an inference variable and deferred obligations.

Attempts to normalize a projection type with recursion detection and projection-cache support, returning either a concrete normalized term, ambiguity, or in-progress recursion. It explicitly calls `project` to compute the projection when cache lookup does not decide the result, and then records progress, ambiguity, or errors back into the cache while extending the caller's obligations.

Produces an error-tolerant normalized term by creating a fresh type or const inference variable and adding the projected trait obligation so trait solving can continue. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Constructs a `Progress` value whose term is an error type and whose obligations list is empty; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Appends additional obligations to an existing `Progress` result and returns it; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Top-level projection solver that checks recursion and prior errors, assembles candidates from the parameter environment, trait definition, object bounds, and impl selection, then either confirms a unique candidate or returns ambiguity/error/no-progress. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_param_env`, `assemble_candidates_from_trait_def`, `assemble_candidates_from_object_ty`, `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, `confirm_candidate`, `Progress::error`, and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`/`ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error` indirectly through candidate assembly outcomes.

Builds a projection candidate for an impl-trait-in-trait associated item by deriving the parent trait predicate and attempting selection with `select` inside `commit_if_ok`. On success it records `ProjectionCandidate::ImplTraitInTrait` via `push_candidate`; on uncertainty it calls `mark_ambiguous`, and on selection failure it calls `mark_error`.
Collects projection candidates from the caller bounds in the parameter environment. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Scans item bounds from the trait definition for matching projection clauses, pushes matching trait-definition candidates, and marks ambiguity when matching cannot be decided. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Builds projection candidates from object type projection bounds when the trait supports object-based projection, and marks ambiguity if the self type is still a type variable. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Filters a stream of projection predicates by associated item and argument compatibility, probes whether each can match the goal, and either pushes a candidate or marks ambiguity. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Selects the underlying trait obligation to derive impl-based projection candidates, then records ambiguity, selection error, or a usable builtin/user-defined candidate while accounting for specialization and builtin trait cases. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error`.

Turns a chosen projection candidate into concrete projected progress by delegating to the appropriate confirmation routine and then opportunistically resolving inferred regions in the resulting term. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` for `ParamEnv`, `Object`, and `TraitDef` candidates, and `confirm_select_candidate` for `Select` candidates.

Confirms an impl-selected candidate by dispatching to the appropriate builtin or user-defined confirmation path based on the selected impl source and trait kind. It calls `confirm_impl_candidate`, `confirm_coroutine_candidate`, `confirm_future_candidate`, `confirm_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_async_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_closure_candidate`, `confirm_fn_pointer_candidate`, `confirm_async_closure_candidate`, `confirm_async_fn_kind_helper_candidate`, and `confirm_builtin_candidate`.

Handles projection for generator associated types (`Yield`/`Return`) by resolving the obligation self type as a generator, normalizing its generator signature with `normalize_with_depth`, building the corresponding generator projection predicate via `generator_trait_ref_and_outputs`, and then delegating final confirmation to `confirm_param_env_candidate`. It returns that result augmented with the incoming nested obligations and the obligations produced during signature normalization via `with_addl_obligations`.

Computes the `Future::Output` projection from the normalized coroutine signature of an async future and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Resolves built-in associated type projections such as discriminant, async destructor, or pointee metadata, building any extra obligations needed, then confirms the resulting projection through the param-env path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.
Normalizes a function pointer signature and confirms its callable output projection via the shared callable path. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Builds the effective callable signature for closures or coroutine-closures, including async/coroutine-specific output construction when needed, then confirms the resulting callable projection. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.
Constructs the `FnOnce::Output` projection predicate from a callable signature and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate`.

Confirms a projection candidate taken from the parameter environment by instantiating the cached binder, normalizing the obligation projection and optionally the candidate projection with `normalize_with_depth_to`, equating the two projections via inference, and on success extending obligations and calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations`; on failure it returns an error term.

Confirms a projection candidate coming from a selected impl by locating the associated item in the impl, rebasing and translating trait/impl arguments, building the resulting associated term from the impl item definition, checking argument compatibility, and then calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations` before instantiating the term; if the impl item is missing or incompatible it returns an error progress.

Checks whether the substitution list matches the associated item's generic parameter structure and argument kinds. It calls `generics_of` to fetch the associated item's generics, `as_slice` to view the substitutions as generic arguments, and then delegates the recursive validation to `check_substs_compatible_inner`.

Recursively validates that a generic argument slice is structurally compatible with a `Generics` definition: it compares `count` against `len`, uses `split_at` to separate parent and local arguments, calls `generics_of` to load parent generics, recursively calls `check_substs_compatible_inner` for the parent chain, and then uses `zip` plus `unpack` to ensure each local argument kind matches its corresponding type, lifetime, or const parameter.

Confirms an impl-trait-in-trait projection by finding the concrete associated definition with `assoc_def`, normalizing the impl method predicates with `normalize_with_depth_to`, converting them into nested obligations, and normalizing the bound impl-trait result type with `normalize_to` before returning the final projected term and obligations.

Collects and adds the associated item's own declared predicates as nested obligations by instantiating the item's predicates, normalizing each predicate with `normalize_with_depth_to`, choosing an appropriate obligation cause, and pushing each normalized predicate as a deeper obligation.

Finds the concrete associated item definition for an impl, first checking the impl's own item map directly and otherwise querying specialization ancestors with `leaf_def`; it returns the matching `LeafDef` or reports an internal bug if no associated item exists.
Trait method contract for deriving a projection-cache key from a poly projection predicate and selection context.

Builds a `ProjectionCacheKey` for a poly projection predicate only when it has no bound vars. It explicitly calls `ProjectionCacheKey::new` after resolving inference variables in the predicate's projection type with `resolve_vars_if_possible`.
Trait method declaration for deeply normalizing a foldable value in the query-based trait-selection context, returning the normalized value plus any generated obligations, or `NoSolution` on failure.

Entry point for query-based deep normalization on `At`: it first checks `needs_normalization`, then builds a `QueryNormalizer`, precomputes escaping-binder universe slots with `visit_with` when needed, runs normalization by calling `try_fold_with` on the input, and finally packages the result and accumulated obligations into `Normalized`.

Visits a binder while tracking escaping bound-variable depth by shifting the current outer binder index inward before recursively visiting the binder contents and shifting it back afterward. It does not call other methods in this file.
Checks whether a visited type contains escaping bound variables beyond the current binder depth and updates the maximum escaping depth when it does. It does not call other methods in this file.
Checks whether a visited late-bound region escapes the current binder depth and updates the maximum escaping depth accordingly. It does not call other methods in this file.

Handles const visitation for escaping-bound-var analysis by updating the maximum escaping depth for bound consts that escape, and otherwise recursively visiting nested const structure. It does not call other methods in this file.
Returns the type context carried by the normalizer’s inference context. It does not call any methods in this file.

Folds under a binder while maintaining parallel universe bookkeeping by pushing a fresh universe slot before recursive folding and popping it afterward. It may recursively invoke this file’s folding methods through `try_super_fold_with`, including `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_ty`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_const`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_predicate`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_binder`, and `QueryNormalizer::tcx` as required by nested contents.

Core type-normalization routine: it skips already-normal types, reuses cached normalized results, recursively folds substructure, normalizes opaque aliases and projection-like aliases through compiler queries, handles escaping bound variables with placeholder replacement, accumulates obligations, enforces recursion limits for opaque expansion, and caches the final normalized type. It calls `QueryNormalizer::tcx` directly, and may recursively call `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_ty`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_const`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_predicate`, and `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_binder` through `try_super_fold_with`/`try_fold_with` while folding nested structure.

Recursively folds a const and then evaluates it in the current inference and parameter-environment context, including replacement of escaping bound variables needed for query-safe evaluation. It may recursively call `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_ty`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_const`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_predicate`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_binder`, and `QueryNormalizer::tcx` through `try_super_fold_with` while folding nested contents.

Normalizes a predicate only when that predicate kind permits normalization and actually requires it; otherwise it returns the predicate unchanged. When normalization is allowed, it may recursively call `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_ty`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_const`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_predicate`, `QueryNormalizer::try_fold_binder`, and `QueryNormalizer::tcx` through `try_super_fold_with`.

Canonicalizes a query input while also preserving universe information for free regions and inference vars, and increments the canonicalization perf counter. Calls `Canonicalizer::canonicalize`.

Canonicalizes a solver/query response using response-specific region handling, creating fresh `OriginalQueryValues` bookkeeping for the result. Calls `OriginalQueryValues::default` and `Canonicalizer::canonicalize`.
Canonicalizes a user type annotation with the stricter user-annotation region policy, using fresh original-value bookkeeping. Calls `OriginalQueryValues::default` and `Canonicalizer::canonicalize`.
Canonicalizes a query while preserving `'static` but abstracting other free regions, and increments the canonicalization perf counter. Calls `Canonicalizer::canonicalize`.
Trait hook that defines how a canonicalization mode rewrites a free region into its canonical form.
Trait hook that reports whether the mode canonicalizes arbitrary free regions, influencing which type flags require traversal.
Trait hook that reports whether the mode preserves universe indices for canonical variables.

Implements response-mode region canonicalization: leaves ordinary free/early-bound/static/erased regions unchanged, converts placeholders and region vars into canonical region variables, and reports unexpected region forms as delayed bugs. Calls `Canonicalizer::canonical_var_for_region`, `Canonicalizer::region_var_universe`, and `ty::tls::with`.
Reports that response canonicalization does not canonicalize arbitrary free regions.
Reports that response canonicalization preserves universe indices.

Implements user-annotation region canonicalization: keeps user-nameable free regions as-is and canonicalizes region inference vars in the root universe, rejecting any other region forms. Calls `Canonicalizer::canonical_var_for_region_in_root_universe`.
Reports that user-type-annotation canonicalization does not canonicalize arbitrary free regions.
Reports that user-type-annotation canonicalization does not preserve universe indices.
Canonicalizes every free region into a canonical region variable in the root universe. Calls `Canonicalizer::canonical_var_for_region_in_root_universe`.
Reports that this mode canonicalizes arbitrary free regions.
Reports that this mode does not preserve universe indices.
Canonicalizes every free region while preserving its original universe. Calls `InferCtxt::universe_of_region` and `Canonicalizer::canonical_var_for_region`.
Reports that this mode canonicalizes arbitrary free regions.
Reports that this mode preserves universe indices.
Leaves `'static` unchanged and canonicalizes every other free region in the root universe. Calls `Region::is_static` and `Canonicalizer::canonical_var_for_region_in_root_universe`.
Reports that this mode canonicalizes arbitrary free regions except for the special `'static` case handled by the region hook.
Reports that this mode does not preserve universe indices.
Returns the `TyCtxt` used by this folder.
Traverses under a binder while updating the current de Bruijn index on entry and exit. Calls `DebruijnIndex::shift_in`, `TypeFoldable::super_fold_with`, and `DebruijnIndex::shift_out`.

Canonicalizes regions during folding: rejects escaping late-bound regions, opportunistically resolves region vars before delegating to the active mode, and forwards other free-like regions directly to the mode hook. Calls `RegionConstraintData::opportunistic_resolve_var`, `TyCtxt::reuse_or_mk_region`, and `CanonicalizeMode::canonicalize_free_region`.

Canonicalizes types by resolving inference vars when possible, creating canonical vars for unresolved type/int/float vars and placeholders, preserving valid bound vars, and recursively folding structured types only when their flags indicate canonicalizable content. Calls `InferCtxt::probe_ty_var`, `CanonicalizeMode::preserve_universes`, `Canonicalizer::canonicalize_ty_var`, and `TypeFoldable::super_fold_with`; it also recursively calls `fold_ty` on resolved inference types.

Canonicalizes consts by resolving inference const vars when possible, creating canonical vars for unresolved const vars and placeholders, preserving valid bound consts, and recursively folding structured consts only when needed. Calls `InferCtxt::probe_const_var`, `CanonicalizeMode::preserve_universes`, `Canonicalizer::canonicalize_const_var`, and `TypeFoldable::super_fold_with`; it also recursively calls `fold_const` on resolved inference consts.

Top-level canonicalization driver: computes which type flags require rewriting from the selected mode, returns a fast-path `Canonical` when nothing needs work, otherwise folds the value with a fresh `Canonicalizer` and builds the final canonical result including interned variable info and max universe. Calls `CanonicalizeMode::any`, `TypeFoldable::has_type_flags`, `List::empty`, `SmallVec::new`, `FxHashMap::default`, `TypeFoldable::fold_with`, `Canonical::unchecked_map`-related value checks via `needs_infer`/`has_placeholders`, `TyCtxt::intern_canonical_var_infos`, and `OriginalQueryValues::universe_canonicalized_variables`.

Interns or reuses a canonical variable for a generic argument, records the original value in query state, preserves and remaps universes when enabled, and uses a small-vector fast path before falling back to the hash map deduplication table. Calls `CanonicalVarInfo::universe` and `CanonicalizeMode::preserve_universes`.

Returns the collected canonical variables, but if multiple universes were recorded it rebuilds the variable list with universes renumbered into canonical query order via a reverse universe map. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Creates a canonical region variable fixed to the root universe for the given region. It explicitly calls `canonical_var_for_region`.
Looks up and returns the universe index assigned to a region inference variable from the region constraints state. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Interns or reuses a canonical variable for a region, then wraps its bound var index as an anonymous late-bound region at the current binder depth and returns the interned region. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Canonicalizes a type inference variable by first shallow-resolving it; if already bound, it recursively canonicalizes the resolved type, otherwise it creates a fresh bound canonical type variable at the current binder. It explicitly calls `fold_ty`.

Canonicalizes a const inference variable by first shallow-resolving it; if already bound, it recursively canonicalizes the resolved const, otherwise it creates a fresh bound canonical const variable and canonicalizes the const's type for the result. It explicitly calls `fold_const` and `fold_ty`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_infer/src/infer/higher_ra: Instantiates the supertype binder with placeholders by calling `instantiate_binder_with_placeholders`, instantiates the subtype binder with fresh inference variables by calling `instantiate_binder_with_fresh_vars`, and then performs the higher-ranked subtype comparison by calling `sub(...).relate(...)` on the instantiated values; it returns `Ok(())` to avoid exposing results that still mention placeholders.

Checks that higher-ranked placeholders do not leak outside `outer_universe`, unless leak checking is disabled. When enabled, it obtains region constraints through `borrow_mut` and `unwrap_region_constraints`, gets the current universe with `universe`, and then delegates to region-constraint `leak_check`.

Returns the binder contents unchanged when `no_bound_vars` finds no bound variables; otherwise creates a fresh universe with `create_next_universe`, builds placeholder regions/types/consts via `mk_region`, `mk_ty`, and `mk_const` using `RePlaceholder`/`Placeholder`, and then calls `replace_bound_vars_uncached` to substitute all bound variables in the binder with those placeholders.

Advances whichever underlying sibling iterator variant is active, forwarding `next()` to either the filtered or unfiltered iterator. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Trait requirement for inserting an impl into a `Children` bucket without overlap or specialization checks; this declaration does not meaningfully call other Methods List methods.

Computes the impl's simplified `Self` type and stores the impl in either `non_blanket_impls` or `blanket_impls` without checking overlap or ordering. It does not call other Methods List methods.
Finds the bucket for an impl from its simplified `Self` type, locates the impl inside that bucket, and removes it. It does not call other Methods List methods.

Searches potential sibling impls, checks overlap, uses specialization ordering to decide whether the new impl is a sibling, should recurse under an existing child, or should replace existing children as a new parent, and returns the corresponding `Inserted` state plus any future-compat lint info. Trait requirement for recording a parent/child impl relation loaded from crate metadata; this declaration does not meaningfully call other Methods List methods.

Inserts a local impl into the specialization graph: it handles erroneous trait refs conservatively at the root, computes the simplified `Self` type, walks down from the trait root by repeatedly delegating per-node placement decisions, and rewires parent/child edges when the new impl becomes a parent of existing nodes. Records an externally supplied parent/child impl relation, rejecting duplicate parent information, then inserts the child into the parent's child bucket. It explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> ChildrenExt<'tcx> for Children::insert_blindly`.
